live.target: Binary and mechanical, from the publisher's own per-year products: positive iff the charity's BN is present in the year-Y 'List of charities' Identification file and absent from the year-Y+1 Identification file. Optional covariates also available at the instant: observed fire-risk grid for day D (NetCDF published ~03:32 server time on D+1) and INPE's forecast risk grids for D+1..D+3 (published on day D). Excluded as post-instant: every detection row with event time > D, and any current-year statistic that only becomes final later. As-of policy: each detection row carries its event timestamp (data_pas / data_hora_gmt); the archive is treated as an append-mostly observation log; LIMITATION (recorded): INPE regenerates archive files (2003-2017 files regenerated 2025-09-08; 2024 file regenerated 2025-06-06) and no historical file vintages are kept, so features are taken from the current archive under the policy that detection rows are immutable observations; construction pins file checksums and must re-fetch one fixed month after >=2 weeks to measure late-row churn before quoting any number.

live.question: A Brazilian municipality has recorded zero active-fire detections (INPE reference-satellite series) for 14 consecutive days through day D. At 13:00 UTC on day D+1 - after INPE's morning consolidation of day-D detections (daily CSV for day D observed published 09:05 BRT on D+1) - given only the municipality's detection history through day D, the calendar, state and biome, will at least one active-fire detection be recorded in that municipality within the next 7 days (event days D+1..D+7)? A useful prediction lets PREVFOGO/IBAMA, state civil defence and municipal fire brigades pre-position crews in a country where detection precedes enforcement, and persistence cannot win by construction.

signoff.baseline_decision_criterion: Runner-contract model eval AUC on the identical 11,791 eval rows vs the unspsc_only reference bar 0.5707 (measured post-acceptance by the build's score.py, to be re-measured independently in the baseline job from the same bytes). Decision basis: the paired difference on identical rows with a publication-day-clustered bootstrap interval (the day is the gate's independence unit); headroom is demonstrated only if the model exceeds the bar and the clustered interval excludes zero. If the model trails the bar or the interval contains zero, record no demonstrated headroom under this protocol.
signoff.decision: RESOLVED - the assisted review is closed by rebuild cl-tender-003; artifact 27e610ba65e13805 is the accepted evidence base and the baseline decision may proceed on it.
reasoning: Finding 3 (label aggregation without a defined terminal state/horizon): repaired and measured. The label is now a deterministic function of a closed, vintage-covered window: award releases dated inside pub+180d are walked in date order and the last terminal status decides (active->adjudicated=0, all-unsuccessful->deserted=1, all-cancelled->revoked); pending is non-terminal; the compiledRelease fallback is dropped and bucketed. HORIZON_DAYS=180 was frozen from measured first-award-release lags (p50 33-41 d, p90 <=102 d) and capped by the zip vintages (holdout latest release 2021-12-30 >= 2021-06-30+180d = 2021-12-27), so 180 d is the maximum uniform horizon the source supports and no split's labels depend on data its vintage lacks. mixed_terminal 0 and duplicate_ocid 0 in every split; awardUpdate-tagged releases are matched (the previous exact-tag filter silently ignored them - caught by the synthetic smoke before worker spend).

Finding 1 (cancelled awards assigned no target, blank targets silently removed): repaired by declaration and measurement. Revoked and right-censored rows are named, counted buckets per split - revoked_rate 0.0286/0.0444/0.0383, censored_rate 0.0453/0.0566/0.0512, scored_share 0.9262/0.8990/0.9105 (train/eval/holdout) - with the unobserved-target decomposition (no_award_within_horizon / award_beyond_horizon / pending_within_horizon) counted from the rows, never inferred. No row leaves the scored files silently.

Finding 2 (selection declared as publication-time-only while actually conditioned on the outcome): repaired by making the declaration true. Membership is decided by publication-time fields only (first tender release month + publication state 'active' + ocid). The scored CSVs are explicitly declared as the OUTCOME-DEPENDENT subset of that membership in quality.json's row_selection basis, which requires the outcome_conditioning rates to be quoted beside any score taken from this artifact. The reopen condition's first clause is satisfied at the membership level; the scored-subset restriction itself cannot be made publication-time-decidable because the outcome is genuinely future, so the review closes on the qualification skill's alternative path: the intended population and observation mechanism are resolved explicitly (fixed horizon, measured per-split rates) instead of being hidden behind a timing-neutral claim.

Scientific acceptability of the conditional population: the prediction instant (publication; features are administrative records written then) strictly precedes the label window (<= pub+180d). Conditioning the task population on reaching an observed terminal state within a fixed horizon is a competing-risks-style conditional prediction task, legitimate when declared with measured rates; the defect the review caught was the false publication-time claim plus the ill-defined any-active label, both now gone. The conditioning is uniform across splits (scored_share 0.90-0.93 everywhere, applied by one rule), so eval/holdout comparisons are not differentially distorted by it; the residual prevalence shift (holdout 25.1% vs train 17.6%) stays documented as a property, and the fixed-horizon rule also avoids the 'terminal at today's snapshot' failure mode - no label depends on when the data was downloaded.
signoff.scope_limitation: Every score from this artifact describes the conditional population only: tenders whose process reaches a terminal adjudicated-or-deserted state within 180 days of publication (~90-93% of eligible rows per split). Deployment over all published tenders would face the excluded revoked (~3-4%) and unresolved-at-180d (~5%) cases this task does not score. Any card or report quoting a score must quote the outcome_conditioning rates beside it (this requirement is written into the accepted quality.json row_selection basis).

T is the latest Fecha row present in the file at fetch. The SIH files are the publisher's cumulative current-vintage archive, not point-in-time snapshots: the portal warns 'Algunas bases de datos pueden incluir actualizaciones retroactivos por lo que la informacion historica puede cambiar en actualizaciones posteriores', and the 1990s show partial backfill (ALRBN volume column 50 percent populated 1990-1999, 100 percent from 2000). Features are therefore stated as current-vintage values, same treatment as the published abs-visitor-arrivals-direction record; no claim of historical operational availability is made (see review). records.question: For a Mexican dam in the CONAGUA SIH reservoir network (210 catalogued dams, 26 states) whose published stored volume VolumenAlm on the latest available day T is at or above the drought threshold (25 percent of the dam's reference capacity), will VolumenAlm fall below that threshold on at least one day in the 30 calendar days after T (a drought-onset event)? A useful prediction supports water-allocation planning, drought-monitoring inputs (the official Monitor de Sequia en Mexico uses reservoir availability as an index), and urban supply outlooks (Monterrey 2022, Tijuana 2019-2022, Falcon 2002 crises all crossed this threshold in this panel).
records.review: Five contracts, reconciled against written evidence: (1) Redistribution SUPPORTED - CC BY 4.0 on the publisher's own resource record (class A), quoted with URL; attribution 'CONAGUA, SIH' carried into LICENSE.md at release. (2) Prediction timing SUPPORTED with documented vintage limitation - the instant is stateable and observed (weekly-updated file; T = latest Fecha, measured 2026-10-26 on a 2026-10-27 fetch; one sampled dam lagged 29 days, so T is measured per dam per fetch); every feature row is Fecha <= T, the whole target window is Fecha > T; current-vintage treatment documented because the publisher warns of retroactive updates and the archive is cumulative (partial 1990s backfill observed) - no historical operational-availability claim, which is what the evaluation contract must state. (3) Target SUPPORTED - label from VolumenAlm(Mm3) rows after T, excludable by date filter; eligibility defined only from information at T (>= 365 prior rows, volume at/above threshold); censoring: missing days recorded as absent rows (no fabricated zero volumes), and right-edge truncation only affects the last 30 days; threshold frame ambiguity identified and bounded - two frames measured, the proxy is the strictly harder threshold, so events under the proxy are a subset of events under the official-capacity frame and capacity holds under both. (4) Split capacity SUPPORTED - 26-dam stratified sample measured from the source: 357 onset events, 202/84/71 across train/eval/holdout, both classes in every window, 271 (dam, year) clusters recorded; the full-panel count is a worker measurement recorded as the first construction step (monotone in dams: additional dams cannot empty a window). (5) Not a mirror SUPPORTED - novelty check recorded with verdict differentiated: prior art ships raw series (ResOpsUS 679 US dams; GROWL 4,134 global series) or closed-data studies (Türkiye, data 'under official permission and commercial terms'); no ML-ready public dam-storage drought-onset prediction task with an as-of policy, splits and a scored contract exists for Mexico or any jurisdiction; this task shape was probed twice before on this bench (tw-reservoir-drought-storage, za-dws-dam-storage-exceedance) and both died on ACCESS, never sourcing the shape - this candidate sources it. Unresolved, recorded: full-panel split counts (worker prerequisite); official per-dam capacities need a proper parse of the weekly-report archive (the PDF text layer is scrambled); intra-day observation cutoff undocumented (contract avoids assuming one); the weekly-summary cell-level cross-check is deferred to construction with the press-figure corroboration standing in its place.

Dams with zero historical onsets at the chosen threshold (4 of the 26 sampled) are an eligibility choice for construction: either exclude or keep as all-negative rows, decided and documented at build time.
records.target: Binary: 1 if VolumenAlm(Mm3) < threshold on at least one day with Fecha in (T, T+30] in the dam's SIH series, else 0. Label source column: VolumenAlm(Mm3) (the same column as the target variable), excluded from features by the Fecha <= T filter; no other column carries the answer. Threshold frame, two candidates measured in the sample: (a) discovery-time proxy = 25 percent of the dam's own observed maximum VolumenAlm (the SIH catalog carries no capacity column); (b) construction-time preferred frame = 25 percent of official capacity, published per dam in CONAGUA's weekly 'Almacenamiento de las Principales Presas del Pais' report (columns CAPACIDAD MUERTA / CAP. UTIL DISENO Mm3; archive at ftp://ftp.conagua.gob.mx/Gobmx/DisponibilidadenPresas/) and in the press-percentage frame (e.g. El Cuchillo capacity 1,123 Mm3 vs observed max 1,765.7 Mm3 including flood surcharge; the proxy threshold 441.4 Mm3 equals 39 percent of the official frame, so the proxy is the conservative/higher threshold and events under it are a subset of events under the official frame). Eligibility at T, from information available at prediction: dam has >= 365 prior daily VolumenAlm rows and VolumenAlm(T) >= threshold (onset formulation; days already below threshold are not prediction rows).

measurements.api_contract_2026_10_19: LDA conventions learned from the API's own error text (each from a 400/404 that named the problem): regime segment is compliance-rBWD (not 'bwd'); the generic /compliance/... prefix does not exist; year-slice and point-slice endpoints are ITEM pages - '_pageSize can only be used with a list endpoint'; assessments live at result.primaryTopic.observation; '?year=...' is 'unrecognised short name or literal: year'.
measurements.caveats_recorded: Small panel by design: ~415-451 entities, 11 label seasons (2020 absent). The label autocorrelates with the prior season's classification (4-year rolling percentile window), so a persistence baseline will be strong; headroom above persistence is the make-or-break measurement and belongs to construction - if measured headroom is nil, record that finding and demote before release. The 2024 Poor jump (18 -> 37) shows genuine year-to-year churn, which is the predictable signal.

review.finding: Persistence dominates the candidate's own information set. The label is a 4-season rolling rBWD percentile, so last season's published classification (used ordinally, not collapsed to a binary) already scores AUC 0.958 on eval and 0.981 on holdout. The apparent gap against binary persistence (0.820) is a scoring-coarseness artefact, not headroom: the better-specified 3-season count reference is worse (0.847/0.941). Constructing this task would demonstrate that copying the previous year works.
review.scope_limits: Pre-launch ceiling on published slices - no gate, no accepted artifact and no fitted model, so this is not the skill's model-vs-persistence measurement and does not establish that no model can exceed 0.958 by a small margin. records.split_strategy: Temporal by reporting cycle: train on early-cycle transitions, eval on middle cycles, holdout on the newest public cycles (2021-2022 provisional / 2022-2023 final at the far end). Both classes are present in every measured cycle window (2023 call: 11.2% positives, 21,537 answered plants, 30 reporters). MEASURED CAVEAT: only the 2022-2023 cycle was downloaded and measured this session (2,411 positives); the 2011-2012, 2021-2022 and any recoverable 2007-2020 cycles are confirmed public only by catalogue/share-link HEAD probes, not by row counts - construction step 1 is to pin the public cycle inventory and measure the uwwCode join rate between at least two cycles. Positives cluster by country reporting regime (measured: any-F rate DE 0.4% vs NO 49.6%), so clustered/stratified counts per split must be reported; a split that puts a country's plants only in train and only in eval would measure regime shift, not plant performance.
records.target: Binary from the source row of cycle N+1: label = 1 iff the plant (uwwState=1, active) has at least one treatment-performance parameter assessed 'F' among the six uww*Perf fields, restricted to plants with at least one answered (P or F) parameter; plants with only NA/NR/blank assessments are unobserved-target rows, counted separately, never dropped silently. Measured on the full 2023 call CSV: 2,411 positives / 21,537 answered (11.2% base rate). The uww*Perf codes are P/F/NA/NR (documented in the Eionet data dictionary element pages, e.g. element 104947 'Treatment performance: BOD5'); the 'In cause of failure' fields (uwwBadPerformance 'Bad performance' 1,765 Yes among active, uwwBadDesign 'Bad design or dimensioning', uwwAccidents 'Major accidents', uwwInformation free text) describe the reported CAUSE where the plant does not meet requirements and are label-source/label-adjacent columns, excluded from features. IMPORTANT measured property recorded as part of the definition: the label is 'REPORTED as failing' - a mixture of physical performance and the national reporting regime; measured 2023-call any-F rates range from DE 0.4% (16/3,776) and BE 2.8% to NO 49.6% (116/234), HR 53.5% (46/86) and RO 36.3% (352/971). Country is therefore a legitimate feature AND the reference baseline must be country-stratified; the mixture is the task's documented semantics, not a defect to hide.

Entities recur across windows by construction (23,708 installation keys observed over 2005-2030 rows), so the row id must be the composite (registry, installation, year) and the recurring-entity property declared, not mistaken for split leakage; positives cluster weakly at the installation level (an installation's net-short status is autocorrelated year to year), so the clustered count to report is distinct installations going net-short in a window, measured at construction.
records.target: Binary, computed from the source row of (installation, year t): VERIFIED_EMISSIONS(t) > ALLOCATION(t), where ALLOCATION is the free allocation recorded in the registry for year t and VERIFIED_EMISSIONS is the independently verified emissions figure. Unit: both are tonnes CO2-equivalent per installation-year (1 allowance = 1 tonne); the comparison is unit-free within the source's own frame (no external threshold or datum is involved). Frame restriction: installation-years where both VERIFIED_EMISSIONS and ALLOCATION are numeric ('n/a' rows - not-yet-operating, excluded or closed sites - are out of frame and their handling must be pinned at construction). Label source columns VERIFIED_EMISSIONS and ALLOCATION at year t are recorded in label_source_columns and must be absent from the shipped features; feature rows may use emissions/allocation/surrender values only for years <= t-1 plus year-t allocation.

records.prediction_time: Instant: 13:00 UTC on day D+1. Features are everything published by then with event time <= D: the complete detection archive through day D (daily file for D observed complete at 09:05 BRT on D+1; detections stream near-real-time at 10-minute granularity during day D), calendar, state/biome. Optional covariates also available at the instant: observed fire-risk grid for day D (NetCDF published ~03:32 server time on D+1) and INPE's forecast risk grids for D+1..D+3 (published on day D). Excluded as post-instant: every detection row with event time > D, and any current-year statistic that only becomes final later. As-of policy: each detection row carries its event timestamp (data_pas / data_hora_gmt); the archive is treated as an append-mostly observation log; LIMITATION (recorded): INPE regenerates archive files (2003-2017 files regenerated 2025-09-08; 2024 file regenerated 2025-06-06) and no historical file vintages are kept, so features are taken from the current archive under the policy that detection rows are immutable observations; construction pins file checksums and must re-fetch one fixed month after >=2 weeks to measure late-row churn before quoting any number.

A useful prediction lets PREVFOGO/IBAMA, state civil defence and municipal fire brigades pre-position crews in a country where detection precedes enforcement, and persistence cannot win by construction.

records.split_strategy: Temporal splits on ISO-week transitions, disjoint and ordered: candidate windows (to be fixed at construction from the full 58-month archive, ~250 weekly transitions 2022-01..2026-10): train on transitions up to 2024-12, eval on 2025 transitions, holdout on 2026 transitions (exact windows fixed at construction). Each weekly transition carries both classes: measured increase rate 15.5%-22.2% and decrease rate 14.5%-20.1% across all 7 measured transitions (Aug-Sep 2026, 10% premise subsample), so class balance holds window-to-window. Positives cluster by item: 54-58 distinct items show >=1 increasing pair per transition, and the top-10 items carry 38-45% of positive pairs - the clustered event count (item-level, not pair-level) must be reported per split and is ~55/week in the subsample (~170/week full panel, estimate). Cross-split identifier policy: item-premise pairs (and premises/items) recur across windows by design - the panel is longitudinal - so entity keys are NOT split-exclusive; the no-cross-split-entities check does not apply to pair panels where the same pair legitimately appears in many weekly transitions. This must be declared in quality.json (expected_duplicate_ids / documented repeats) at construction, mirroring the runner-contract handling of longitudinal panels.
records.target: Binary: modal(price of item i at premise p over all observations in ISO week W+1) > modal(same over week W). Modal price = most frequent observed price that week (ties broken by higher price, deterministic). Pairs with <3 observations in either week are excluded from that transition's rows (exclusion is a function of data through week W+1, applied identically everywhere; it affects ~3% of subsample pairs). The label source columns are the W+1 price observations themselves: no price observation with date > end of week W may ship as a feature column; the shipped target is 0/1.

measurements.probe_defect_correction_2026_10_21: CORRECTION 2026-10-21 (construction session): the discovery panel probe (probe_panel.py) had two defects that silently shrank its panel, and every figure below was recomputed on the corrected load (build.py --source-dir over the same 102 CSVs; script .factory/nhsae_recompute.py, command and output in notes.md). Defect 1: the probe opened files with encoding="utf-8", so the five BOM-prefixed files (July 2019, August 2021, July/August/September 2023) keyed Period as "\ufeffPeriod", d.get("Period") returned "" and five whole months were dropped (probe printed '1,152 non-monthly rows' where the true count is 101 TOTAL rows; 1,051 were BOM-file rows). Defect 2: the probe looked up "A&E attendances Type 1", but the 2018-04..2020-03 files name the column "Number of A&E attendances Type 1", so att1 parsed as 0 for 24 months and no provider-month before 2020-04 ever passed the volume gate - the recorded '97 months' panel in fact had no qualifying month before 2020-04. The corrected build reads utf-8-sig and normalises the 'Number of' prefix: 102 months 2018-04..2026-09 (every month the year pages carry), 21,548 provider-months, 134 providers with >= 24 qualifying months, 12,765 qualifying provider-months.
measurements.publisher_cdn_datacenter_block: Measured 2026-10-21: www.england.nhs.uk (CloudFront) serves HTTP 202 with an empty body to the Hetzner worker IP (65.21.158.17, from both servers tried), for every year page; the same URLs serve 200/82,127 B with 12 CSV links to the coordinator under three User-Agent variants. Consequence: construction jobs cannot fetch this publisher from a worker; the 102 CSVs are fetched on the coordinator (measured 3.1 MB total) and staged in the private staging repo, and the job consumes them with per-file sha256 verification. The build's default HTTP path remains for reproducing from an unblocked network.
measurements.revision_policy_measured: Re-measured 2026-10-21 at construction: across the 102 monthly CSVs there are NO duplicate (org, month) keys - each calendar month is published in exactly one file (originals are replaced on the year page by their '...revised...' successor, e.g. April-2020-revised-260421), so the recorded 'keep max Type 1 attendances' dedup never operated on anything. records.split_strategy: Temporal by issue year, all three windows contiguous and disjoint. Proposed: train 2008-2018 (storm-based polygons began Oct 2007), eval 2019-2021, holdout 2022-2024. Anchor measurements support capacity but window totals are computed at construction: measured 2013 = 1,832 warnings / 441 verified (24.1%) spread over 100 distinct days with >=1 verified warning; measured 2023 = 2,531 / 656 (25.9%) over 115 distinct days. Positives cluster by outbreak day, so the clustered count (100-115 independent positive days per measured year) is the figure that matters for window capacity, not the row count. Base-rate drift is a documented property of the source (warning POD peaked 2011, declined 2012-14, then recovered - WAF-D-23-0153), so multi-year windows and a drift note are required, not a single-year holdout.
records.target: Binary: the per-warning `verify` boolean returned by IEM cow for phenomena=TO, significance=W - whether >=1 tornado local storm report (buffered by cow's default 15 km) falls inside the polygon during the valid window. The method is documented on the cow page ('NWS Storm Based Warning Verification') and matches the official storm-based verification concept in NWS Instruction 10-1601 ('FAR is the number of false alarms (unverified warnings) divided by the total number of warnings'; storm report points verify warning areas).

records.target: Would have been a binary change target on a country/city x period indicator series (e.g. quarter-over-quarter rise in a short-term indicator), because a level target on a persistent series is the measured nhs-ae failure mode. records.review: Five contracts reconciled 2026-10-23 on written evidence: (1) Redistribution SUPPORTED - publisher's own instruments (HDX package record CC BY 3.0 IGO with grant and Section 4 quoted; RDF methodology CC BY 4.0), class A, conditions carried to LICENSE.md. (2) Timing SUPPORTED with documented current-vintage assumption - annual instant = first refresh carrying year-D data (observed cadence; 2026-08-20 file carries data through 2025); the task is an explicitly-labelled publication-lag NOWCAST (abs-visitor-arrivals-direction precedent): the target value is unpublished and unavailable on the channel at the instant, while the target year itself has partially elapsed - no 'window follows the instant' claim is made; the archive is revised in place, so values are construction-time vintage, sha256-pinned, the same accepted posture as abs-visitor-arrivals-direction; a future standing vintage collector is NOT needed for the annual task but would strengthen the as-of claim if ever added. records.target: Binary exceedance: label 1 iff the corridor-year (D+1, O, H) government-procedure persons total (sum of all application-type rows; a missing corridor row with the host still reporting counted as 0 applications) is >= 2 x the corridor-year (D, O, H) total. Label source: the same 'Number of Applications' column of the HDX CSV at year D+1; the year-D+1 value and everything derived from it are excluded from shipped features. Censoring: corridors whose host reports no G/P rows at all in D+1 (33 of 7,622 eligible rows, 0.43%) are excluded as unobserved targets, not counted as 0. Note what the target does NOT measure: temporary-protection registrations (e.g. Ukrainians in the EU from 2022) are not asylum applications and do not enter this stream.

records.split_strategy: Temporal, by label year (year_end), computed from the actual audit_opinion_facts CSV (command: python3 candidates/za-municipal-audit-opinion/probe_label_stats.py <audit_opinions.csv>, scratch kept this session): train 2011-2017 = 1,863 rows / 878 positives (47.13%); eval 2018-2020 = 738 rows / 376 positives (50.95%); holdout 2021-2024 = 982 rows / 415 positives (42.26%). Both classes present in every one of the 14 label years (measured per-year rates 35.0%-56.5%). Clustered positives: audit outcomes correlate within an audit cycle/year, so the independence scale is ~14 label years, not 3,689 rows - confidence intervals must be clustered by year and the onset-conditioned variant recomputed at construction. Municipalities are repeated entities across years: features may include each municipality's own history, and the runner's id_columns handle the municipality code; no cross-split entity leakage arises because splits are by time, but the descriptor must declare expected duplicate ids.
records.target: Binary label from the audit_opinions cube ('Code' column, bulk CSV audit_opinion_facts on munimoney-media S3): 1 = qualified, disclaimer or adverse; 0 = unqualified or unqualified_emphasis_of_matter; 'outstanding' rows (audit not completed) are excluded, not imputed. Label source column is never shipped as a feature: the label CSV is used only to build y; features come from the separate incexp/cflow/capital/bsheet/grants/uifwexp/repmaint/aged-debtor/aged-creditor cubes and the demographics API. Measured per-year positive rates (qualified-or-worse, outstanding excluded): 35.0%-56.5% across all 14 label years, never degenerate. Measured persistence: 83.88% year-over-year agreement (2018-2020), so the level label is persistence-shaped and the primary task is the deterioration-onset conditioning; onset base rate measured 69/381 = 18.1% of clean-prev municipality-years in 2018-2020.

The task therefore makes NO claim of operational point-in-time availability for pre-restatement instants (2000-2026.09 history is the 2026-09 restated basis, which demonstrably differs from what was published at those instants - see restatement_2026). records.prediction_time: Instant = the announced embargo lift of the P0043.1 monthly release for reference month M (date+time published in advance by Stats SA; observed publication dates all fall in the last week of month M+1 at 14:30 SAST, lag 25-34 days after month end). At that instant, the latest published reference month is M; month M+1 is partially elapsed (the instant falls inside it), so M+1 can be neither feature nor target; the target month M+2 begins after the instant (about 4 days after) and ends about 34 days after it. Features are the released series values for months <= M only (current-vintage policy; see measurements.restatement_2026 and measurements.intra_basis_revisions). Dated example (Africa/Johannesburg): instant 2026-10-28 14:30 (embargo of the Release 2026-09 issue); feature window 2000-01..2026-09 as released in that vintage (first-available version = the monthly release; values for months M-11..M used by the label's trailing median are the values published at or before the instant); eligibility cutoff = series values for months <= 2026-09 exist; prediction instant 2026-10-28 14:30; target window 2026-11-01 through 2026-11-30 (starts 3 days 9.5 hours after the instant; ends 33 days 9.5 hours after). No part of the target window precedes the instant.

records.question: At the publication instant of the Stats SA P0043.1 'Statistics of liquidations' release for reference month M (published in the last week of month M+1, embargo lifting 14:30 SAST = 12:30 UTC; observed: 25 Mar 2026 for Feb issue, 27 May 2026 for Apr issue, 30 Sep 2026 14:30 for Aug issue, expected 28 Oct 2026 for Sep issue), will the number of liquidations in month M+2 for a given unit (companies/close-corporations x compulsory/voluntary x industry) exceed that unit's trailing 12-month median count over months M-11..M? Prospective users: credit and insurance exposure monitors, procurement/counterparty risk teams, and macro early-warning analysts, who get a ~1-month lead on industry-level insolvency pressure for provisioning and review decisions.
records.review: All five discovery contracts reconciled against recorded evidence. (1) Redistribution: class B - Stats SA permits applying, publishing and distributing the data with attribution, plus a no-sale condition our free releases satisfy (quoted in license_evidence; to be carried into LICENSE.md). (2) Prediction timing: instant = the announced embargo (measured on four issues; always last week of M+1 at 14:30 SAST), M+2 target window entirely after the instant; feature meanings documented by the publisher (export headers + release explanatory notes); vintage contract handled explicitly - the 2026 restatement is measured (110/110 months checked differ from the old basis), pre-restatement vintages are unrecoverable, so the task is a clearly-labelled current-vintage retrospective panel with no operational point-in-time claim for history; intra-basis revision tail measured (19/15,040, all recent months, +1..+7). (3) Target: derived from the published count series itself; label source column excludable by shipping lagged features only; recent-tail revisions noted. (4) Split capacity: measured - both classes in all three windows and all 26 years; independence scale is the month (~306 instants), within-month cross-unit dependence documented as the cluster. (5) Contribution: no ML-ready formulation of SA liquidation counts at any grain found in catalog or literature searches; nearest prior art is firm-level bankruptcy prediction (US/Italian firm panels), a different population and target; novelty check recorded by script. Residual uncertainty: future restatements of the same scale would change future basis (publisher warning observed and quoted); the construction must enforce a restricted prediction protocol against the abs-oad-style cross-row self-answer join (a row's label operand count(M+2) is a feature window value of the row whose target is M+4).

records.split_strategy: Temporal, by target month, computed from the fetched Release-2026-09 panel (command: python3 candidates/za-statsa-liquidations-exceedance/probe_base_rates.py, scratch 2026-10-27): population = 40 industry-level units (companies x compulsory/voluntary x 9 industries, close corporations x compulsory/voluntary x 9 industries) plus the 4 group totals; target month = reference month + 2 (M+2 frame). Median-exceedance label (trailing 12-month median > 0 filter): train target years 2002-2016 = 3,910 rows / 1,537 positives (39.3%), 30/40 units with positives; eval 2017-2020 = 992 / 426 (42.9%), 25/40; holdout 2021-2026 = 1,415 / 574 (40.6%), 24/40. YoY-direction label: train 4,748 / 1,980 (41.7%) 40/40 units, eval 1,206 / 568 (47.1%) 39/40, holdout 1,706 / 739 (43.3%) 39/40. Both classes present in every window and in every year 2001-2026 (positive months per year = 9-12 of 12). Clustering: the independence scale is the MONTH, not the row - 40 units share each month's macro shock, so ~306 scorable monthly instants over 26 years (2002-01..2026-09 minus warmup) are the effective sample; confidence intervals must be clustered by target month. No cross-split entity leakage: splits are by time; units repeat across months by design (panel task, runner id_columns carry the unit code).
records.target: Binary: count of liquidations for unit u in month M+2 (LIQ series value, 'Actual figures', number) > median of u's counts over months M-11..M (both operands from the same current-basis vintage; label source column = the unit's monthly count series itself, which is also the feature source - a row's shipped features are lagged values only, months <= M, never the target month's value). Alternative measured formulation: YoY direction (M+2 count > M-10 count). Trailing-median rows with median 0 (sparse series, all-zero window) are excluded as unlabelable; measured exclusion ~32% of unit-months under the 40-unit population.

(3) Target SUPPORTED - label from the same source column at D+1, excluded from features; observed absence (missing row, active host) = 0; host-silent rows (0.43%) excluded as censored. (4) Split capacity SUPPORTED - disjoint windows with both classes in every label-year, counts and clustered (origin, label-year) counts computed from the source. (5) Not a mirror SUPPORTED - no ML-ready corridor-grain UNHCR benchmark with fixed temporal splits and a scored contract found; prior art is origin-level or EU-bilateral monthly forecasting papers and raw-panel repackages. LIMITATION recorded: the machine-fetchable extract is annual; the RDF's monthly grain stays browser-only behind the WAF, so no monthly variant is buildable from this path. The old park reason (no machine-fetchable bulk path) is resolved by the HDX global package; the correction of the 2026-10-20 search miss is recorded in both sources[1].access and measurements.

packaged.split_strategy: Temporal split on corridor-year label windows (Government procedure, persons, sum of all application-type rows; eligibility: year-D corridor total >= 500 and host active in D+1). Candidate partition, counts computed from the source 2026-10-23: train label-years 2001-2016: n=3,677 rows, 302 positives (x2 prevalence 8.2%), 198 distinct (origin, label-year) positive clusters; eval label-years 2017-2021: n=1,918, 166 positives (8.7%), 109 clusters; holdout label-years 2022-2025: n=1,994, 234 positives (11.7%), 135 clusters. Both classes present in every label-year of every window (positives per label-year range 2-92). Surge origins differ across windows (train: SYR/AFG/IRQ; eval: VEN/AFG/COD; holdout: TUR/VEN/IND/AFG/CUB). Construction may adjust boundaries inside this measured envelope but must recompute and record counts on the frozen artifact; the prevalence drift (more surges later) is a property of the period, to document at construction.
packaged.target: Binary exceedance: label 1 iff the corridor-year (D+1, O, H) government-procedure persons total (sum of all application-type rows; a missing corridor row with the host still reporting counted as 0 applications) is >= 2 x the corridor-year (D, O, H) total. Label source: the same 'Number of Applications' column of the HDX CSV at year D+1; the year-D+1 value and everything derived from it are excluded from shipped features. Censoring: corridors whose host reports no G/P rows at all in D+1 (33 of 7,622 eligible rows, 0.43%) are excluded as unobserved targets, not counted as 0. Note what the target does NOT measure: temporary-protection registrations (e.g. Ukrainians in the EU from 2022) are not asylum applications and do not enter this stream.

measurements.censoring_measured_2026_10_23: Host-year activity: 67 hosts report in 2000 growing to ~110 in recent years; among 7,622 eligible corridor-years, 7,589 (99.57%) have an active host in D+1 (missing corridor row = observed zero) and 33 (0.43%) have a host reporting nothing at all in D+1 (unobserved target; excluded). Absence of a row is treated as zero applications only when the host is still reporting.
measurements.dead_channels_2026_10_20: http://popstats.unhcr.org/en/overview -> HTTP 000 (host gone); https://data.unhcr.org/en/index -> HTTP 404. The pre-RDF population database channel no longer exists.
measurements.deep_links_2026_10_20: The homepage's five export deep links (extracted from the rendered page): population by country of origin (?v2url=dc36b6), population by host country (?v2url=bd1059), demographics of refugees (?v2url=d3e49d), solutions 2015-2024 (?v2url=d63e73), new asylum applications during 2024 (?v2url=1e3087). Navigating a real tab to the origin deep link opens the interactive Data Finder app with that dataset preselected - the URL is a view selector, not a file.
measurements.duplicate_rows_resolved_2026_10_23: 20,851 of 73,051 G/P corridor-year cells (28.5%) carry multiple rows with the same (Year, Origin, Asylum, Procedure, ApplicationType, DataType) key but different counts (e.g. 2000 AFG->DEU G/V/P: 5,380 vs 5,756; 2000 AFG->AUS G/V/C: 90 vs 1,326). Identical rows in all other columns; present in every year incl. 2025 (35 groups), and identical in the per-country extracts (verified on asylum_applications_residing_deu.csv). Resolution rule: SUM all G/P rows per corridor-year. Basis: cross-checks against the primary national publisher's own published host-year totals (BAMF, which is UNHCR's source for Germany) match the sum-all rule to within 0.005-0.09% in four different years, while the max-rule matches BAMF's first-application figure - i.e. the duplicate rows are disjoint components (first vs follow-up applications) exported under one type code, so summing reconstructs the total. See bamf_cross_check_2026_10_23.
measurements.hdx_bulk_path_2026_10_23: HDX package unhcr-population-data-for-world (created 2020-08-27, maintained by the UNHCR organisation account) carries the full global corridor panel in five CSVs. Applications resource: 1 GET (HTTP 302 -> signed URL, curl -L), 200 OK, 8,669,567 bytes, 2.06 s from the coordinator (1.9 GiB class); sha256 d5808616c3d10d33925d4df5a3182a2028dd574d111e843cc207455ba45fe950 identical across two fetches. This resolves the 2026-10-20 access blocker: the 2026-10-20 note 'HDX does not unblock the bulk data' was a search-visibility miss and is corrected here with the package URL.
measurements.hdx_mirrors_2026_10_20: HDX CKAN search 'unhcr population' -> 860 results, of which the full origin-year population series is absent; only per-country extracts (CC BY) and GIS reference layers. 'refugee data finder' search -> 3,427 results, none the full series. HDX does not unblock the bulk data.
measurements.known_event_fixtures_2026_10_23: Reproduced by candidates/unhcr-refugee-data-finder/probe_hdx_asylum_fixture.py (exit 0): SYR->DEU 2014->2015 41,100 -> 162,510 x2 label TRUE (2015 Syrian surge into Germany); AFG->USA 2021->2022 533 -> 25,082 TRUE (post-Aug-2021 Taliban takeover, Afghan asylum filings in the US); AFG->DEU 2021->2022 37,245 -> 48,602 FALSE (large growth, sub-doubling). Anti-fixture recorded: UKR->POL 2021->2022 458 -> 1,593 is below the 500 eligibility at D, and Ukrainians in the EU mostly registered temporary protection rather than asylum applications - the target does not measure temporary-protection registrations.
measurements.label_family_measured_2026_10_23: On eligible corridor-years (G/P sum-all >= 500 at D, host active in D+1; n=7,589 across 2000-2024): decline (D+1 < D) 57.3%; growth >25% 27.4%; growth >50% 18.5%; >=2x 9.3%; >=3x 4.2%. Chosen label: >=2x (doubling), a ~9% prevalence exceedance target in the house family of the other published exceedance tasks. Alternatives measured and recorded; construction must not re-tune the threshold after seeing scores.
measurements.panel_shape_measured_2026_10_23: Applications CSV: 120,597 data rows, 13 columns, years 2000-2025 (26), 215 origin codes, 130 asylum-country codes. Columns: Year, Country of Origin Code/Name, Country of Asylum Code/Name, Procedure Type/Name, Application Type Code/Name, Application Data Type/Data, Application Average Persons Per Case (all zero), Number of Applications (all integer). No month column. Provenance mix (skill requirement): Procedure G=105,862 / U=13,955 / J=780 rows; Data Type P=113,635 / C=6,962. The task is defined on the G/P stream only (99,281 rows, 6,936 distinct corridors, 33.7M applications); the UNHCR-procedure stream (13,640 persons rows) is a separate RSD population, not summed in, and the task does not cover corridors served only by UNHCR procedure.
measurements.recency_2026_10_20: The RDF homepage reports 'Forcibly displaced people worldwide at end-2025: 117.8 million' with charts spanning 2000-2025, so the series is maintained to end-2025 (annual grain) - current and republished on a rolling schedule.
measurements.reporting_model_mix_2026_10_23: Two reporting models inside the G/P stream: split-type codes (N/R/A/J/...) vs unsplit 'V' rows. Measured on eligible corridor-years: train window 1,238 V-model / 2,439 split-model; eval 1,918/0 V-model; holdout 1,994/0 V-model. The eval and holdout windows are 100% split-model; V-model ambiguity therefore touches only training-era rows, and the sum-all rule is cross-checked against BAMF in exactly that era. Type coexistence measured: V never coexists with N/R/A in the same corridor-year (0 of 73,051), so V is an unsplit total, not an additive category; N-with-NR/RA/SP coexistence is rare (646 cells differ between sum-all and a V/NR-preferring rule; 196 eligible).
measurements.split_window_counts_2026_10_23: x2 label, computed from the source: train label-years 2001-2016 n=3,677 / 302 positives / 198 (origin, label-year) positive clusters; eval 2017-2021 n=1,918 / 166 / 109; holdout 2022-2025 n=1,994 / 234 / 135. Positives per label-year: train 2-53, eval 6-57, holdout 26-92; every label-year of every window carries both classes. For comparison, the parked annual origin-grain derivative (unicef-sdmx-refugee-origin-growth) carried only 34 positive origin-years in eval.
measurements.update_cadence_observed_2026_10_23: HDX package activity (CKAN package_activity_list, 60 entries read 2026-10-23): resource/dataset updates on 2025-11-05, 2026-02-25, 2026-06-11, 2026-06-19, 2026-06-22, 2026-08-20 - a several-times-a-year refresh pattern aligned with UNHCR's annual statistical cycle (Global Trends lands ~June of D+1). The 2026-08-20 applications resource carries complete data through 2025, so year-D data is machine-observable at latest ~August of D+1; the conservative instant is the first observed mid-year-or-later refresh carrying year D.

pending.prediction_time: Annual publication-lag NOWCAST - the accepted abs-visitor-arrivals-direction pattern, and it must not be described as a future-event forecast. The prediction instant is the publication of year-D complete annual data on the machine-fetchable channel: UNHCR's annual statistical cycle lands mid-year in D+1 (Global Trends), and the HDX distribution of this dataset was observed refreshing on 2025-11-05, 2026-02-25, 2026-06-11, 2026-06-19, 2026-06-22 and 2026-08-20, with the 2026-08-20 resource carrying complete data through 2025. At that instant every feature is a corridor-year total for years <= D. The target year D+1 has PARTIALLY ELAPSED at the instant (the 2026-08-20 instant lies inside target year 2026, which started 2026-01-01) but its value is entirely UNPUBLISHED: on this channel no D+1 value exists until ~mid-D+2, and for most non-EU hosts no public monthly corridor data exists at all (Eurostat monthly data covers EU hosts only and is outside this channel's shipped features). So the claim recorded here is value-unavailability at the instant, not that the target window follows the instant. A strictly-future variant (at the same instant, predict year D+2 >= 2x the last PUBLISHED year D) was considered and rejected at discovery: the doubling baseline must be published at the instant, so a strict future window forces a two-year-back comparison, a different label and different measured base rates - a different task. The HDX archive is revised in place (current-vintage), so construction pins the fetched snapshot by sha256 and states values as construction-time vintage - the same documented posture as abs-visitor-arrivals-direction. Dated example in notes.md.
